newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch gets tax break to stay in New York City.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch gets tax break to stay in New York City.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc., the nation's biggest stockbroker, will get more than $27 million in tax breaks in exchange for its pledge to stay in New York City and add up to 2,000 jobs under a deal announced Friday.

The 15-year deal, negotiated over three months, provides for $17 million in sales tax exemptions if New York-based Merrill maintains its current city work force of 9,000, plus an additional $10.6 million if Merrill creates the additional 2,000 jobs, the city's Economic Development Corp. said.
The brokerage said it will also buy a 700,000-square-foot office building on Broadway near its lower Manhattan headquarters to consolidate and expand offices scattered throughout the city.
If the company fails to maintain the promised job level, the agreement calls for the repayment or reduction of some or all of the benefits along with penalties.

A source familiar with the negotiations said that while Merrill Lynch had considered moving some workers to New Jersey, it had never considered moving its headquarters to Jersey City, N.J., across the Hudson River, as the city's Economic Development Corp. maintained in its announcement of the package.
New Jersey and New York have conducted frequent "border wars" in past years as each state sought to lure corporate jobs with packages of tax incentives.

"We are continuing to nurture a business climate in New York City which is increasingly irresistible to such major corporations as Merrill Lynch," Mayor Rudolph Giuliani said in a statement. "And these efforts are making it increasingly difficult for places like New Jersey to lure away New York City jobs."

But the source familiar with the talks said the 2,000 jobs, many of them in computers and other technical areas, would be only a small part of Merrill's projected job growth over that period. The source said the company is expected to conduct substantial hiring internationally.

The source said Merrill will probably also add workers in New Jersey, where it employs 9,000 people in back-office processing, customer service, mutual fund management and other areas. The most likely site would be in the Plainsboro, N.J., area, where the company wants to consolidate some facilities.

Including the Merrill agreement, Giuliani's administration has retained 29 major companies representing 70,852 jobs retained and a projected 25,560 new jobs over the next 10 to 20 years, the city's development arm said. The total city tax revenue generated by these companies exceeds $1.1 billion.
In 1996, Merrill's global stock and bond underwriting totalled $187 billion, about 12.9 percent of the world market.
